title: HoverCard
wrapsNative: contextMenu(menuItems:preview:), which shows the preview card on a touch and hold (and a secondary click with a pointer)
summary: A preview card for a link, such as a person or a document, is the system context menu with a custom preview, opened by touching and holding. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To let people peek at what a link points to (a profile, a ticket, a file) and act on it, without opening it.
whenNotToUse: Never for anything essential: touch has no hover and many people never touch and hold. Put the same information one tap away (the link itself, or an info button with a popover, see info-tooltip).
api: func contextMenu<M: View, P: View>(menuItems: () -> M, preview: () -> P) -> some View
func contentShape(_ kind: ContentShapeKinds, _ shape: some Shape) -> some View

states.name: resting
states.description: The link looks like any link.

states.name: previewing
states.description: After a touch and hold the system lifts the preview card above a blurred screen, with the menu items under it. A tap on the preview can open the destination.

appearance: The system draws the lift, the blur and the menu. The preview is the app's view: give it the theme's raised background and Monarch components so it matches the theme in light, dark and both high-contrast modes.
platformNotes: The web HoverCard opens after a delay on pointer hover or keyboard focus and closes when both leave. Touch has no hover, so iOS uses the touch-and-hold context menu, which also opens with a secondary click on a pointer. There is no delay to set. With a pointer on iPad, onHover could open a popover, but a popover then takes the next tap, so it is not recommended. Android composes the same idea from a long-press gesture.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver offers the context menu actions in the rotor of the link, so the actions are reachable without the gesture; the preview itself is not read.
Keep the link's own action (a tap) as the main way to the content.
Text in the preview scales with Dynamic Type; keep it short so it fits.
edgeCases: The preview sizes to its content; give it a width with frame(idealWidth:) for long text.
A context menu with no items still shows the preview.
Set contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, …) so the lifted shape matches the link's background.
